plan.summary: The camera exhibits a no-power condition following extensive shutter cycles (~400,000 actuations). Reported battery terminal voltage does not eliminate power delivery faults under load or safety interlock disengagement.

hypotheses.mechanism: Door or compartment microswitch failure or improper engagement preventing power-on circuit completion
hypotheses.why: DSLR bodies typically incorporate physical interlock microswitches on the battery door and card slot door that cut logic power when open or unseated.
hypotheses.safe_test: Visually inspect the mechanical levers and tabs of the battery and memory card doors to confirm they fully depress their corresponding internal interlock switches when closed.

hypotheses.mechanism: Power delivery failure under load (e.g., degraded battery cells or high-resistance battery terminal contacts)
hypotheses.why: Open-circuit resting voltage measurement on a lithium-ion battery does not confirm capacity or the ability to deliver operating current under load.
hypotheses.safe_test: Test the camera using a known-working, OEM-compatible battery or official DC coupler power adapter without opening the internal chassis.

hypotheses.mechanism: Internal mainboard DC-DC power converter or blown surface-mount fuse failure
hypotheses.why: High total usage or an electrical fault during prolonged operation can open an internal surface-mount fuse or damage power management circuitry, resulting in complete failure to power on.
hypotheses.safe_test: Non-intrusively verify if any status LEDs flash or if the device draws quiescent current when connected via an approved external power adapter.

plan.next_safe_check: Perform a clean external inspection of the battery door and card slot door latches to ensure physical microswitch actuator tabs are intact and fully closing.
plan.uncertainty: Claims regarding prior internal inspection and battery health are unverified anecdotal reports; internal circuitry condition remains unconfirmed without non-destructive diagnostic power testing.
